_readme: YOUR HOLDINGS. This is the file you edit. Save it and the dashboard rebuilds
itself within about a minute.
THE SYMBOLS ARE YOURS - taken from your TradingView Portfolio list and checked
against Yahoo. THE QUANTITIES AND BUY PRICES ARE PLACEHOLDERS. While
'is_example' is true the dashboard shows an orange banner saying so. Put in
your real numbers, set is_example to false, and the banner disappears.
SYMBOL MAPPING - TradingView writes these differently from Yahoo:
TradingView   ->  Yahoo        what it is
AMD           ->  AMD          US stock
MP            ->  MP           US stock
LITE          ->  LITE         US stock
CHZUSDT       ->  CHZ-USD      crypto: USDT pairs become -USD
INJUSDT       ->  INJ-USD      crypto
XAUUSD        ->  GC=F         gold. Yahoo has no spot gold feed, so this is
the futures price - normally a few dollars
above spot. Use GLD instead if you hold the ETF.
BIST:THYAO    ->  THYAO.IS     Borsa Istanbul, if you add Turkish shares
EACH HOLDING NEEDS:
name       - whatever you want to call it
symbol     - the YAHOO symbol. The only field that must be exact.
quantity   - how many shares or coins. Decimals are fine for crypto.
buy_date   - YYYY-MM-DD, the day you bought
buy_price  - what you paid PER SHARE OR COIN, in that market's own currency
where      - free text, a note to yourself
CURRENCY: .IS symbols are priced in lira, everything else in dollars. They are
converted at the live USD/TRY rate before anything is added up, because adding
lira to dollars would produce a meaningless total. Set reporting_currency to
"USD" or "TRY" - it changes how totals are shown, never what you own.
TO EDIT WITHOUT THE TERMINAL:
1. Open https://github.com/firdevssaygin/market-brief
2. Click positions.json, then the pencil icon
3. Change the numbers, scroll down, click 'Commit changes'
4. Wait about a minute and reload your dashboard
Adding and removing holdings works the same way. If you break the formatting -
a missing comma is the usual one - the dashboard tells you which line rather
than silently showing wrong figures.
